title: HDMI 2.1 receiver video capture: TMDS decode and frame write to memory over AXI4
features: TMDS 8b/10b decode of three channels (tmds_ch0..2, one 10-bit character per clock per channel); control tokens on channel 0 give HSYNC / VSYNC, video guard bands are skipped.
CMD.arm starts a capture at the next VSYNC: line k of V_ACTIVE goes to FB_ADDR + k * STRIDE (H_ACTIVE words).
Short lines are padded with zeros and long lines cut (STATUS.len_err); a full line FIFO drops pixels (STATUS.ovf, OVF interrupt).
hpd follows CTRL.hpd_en (hot-plug detect to the source).

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a job ended that saw an AXI error response

sequence: Write CTRL.hpd_en = 1, FB_ADDR, GEOM and V_ACTIVE.
Wait for DONE, check STATUS.len_err / ovf, write 1s to IRQ_STATUS.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time.
tmds_ch0..2 (in) and hpd (out) are the link pins; the TMDS clock is the core clock (one character per clock). FRL (HDMI 2.1 fixed rate link) framing is out of scope: this is the TMDS mode.
The core testbench prints one `LAT <master> dram R|W <cycles>` line per AXI burst (tb/tv_lat_mon.svh), the regression suite's latency format.
